references.text: In the previous verse, Jesus tells us that Satan has demanded to sift the disciples like wheat. Jesus' intercession in verse 32 is the answer to this threat. [ref:Luk 22:31|Luke 22:31] provides the immediate context for Jesus' intercession for Peter.

In Jesus' high priestly prayer, he asks the Father to keep the disciples, just as in [ref:Joh 17:9-11|John 17:9-11] he prays specifically for those the Father has given him. Both passages concern Jesus' intercession for his disciples.
In [ref:Joh 17:15|John 17:15], Jesus asks that the Father keep the disciples from the evil one, which reflects Jesus' intercession for Peter that his faith should not fail.

[ref:Heb 7:25|Hebrews 7:25] speaks of Jesus always living to make intercession for those who come to God through him, which is a continuation of what we see in Luke 22:32 where Jesus prays for Peter's faith.
[ref:Rom 8:34|Romans 8:34] describes Christ at the right hand of God making intercession for us, a theme that directly connects to Jesus' intercession for Peter.
[ref:1 Joh 2:1|1 John 2:1] refers to Jesus as our advocate (parakletos) with the Father, reflecting the same role of intercession that Jesus exercises for Peter in Luke 22:32.

After the resurrection, Jesus restores Peter and commissions him to feed his lambs and sheep ([ref:Joh 21:15-17|John 21:15-17]). This corresponds to the commission "strengthen your brothers" in Luke 22:32, after Peter has turned back.

Peter calls for repentance in [ref:Apg 3:19|Acts 3:19], using the same word (ἐπιστρέφω) that Jesus used when he said "when you have turned back." Peter, who himself repented, now calls others to repentance.
In [ref:Apg 15:32|Acts 15:32], the prophets strengthen (ἐστήρισαν) the brothers, using the same verb (στηρίζω) that Jesus uses when he says "strengthen your brothers" in Luke 22:32.

[ref:1 Pet 5:8-10|1 Peter 5:8-10] warns against the devil and encourages believers to stand firm in their faith. Peter, who himself was strengthened after his denial, now encourages other believers—a direct fulfillment of Jesus' words about strengthening the brothers.

In [ref:1 Pet 5:10|1 Peter 5:10], Peter uses the verb στηρίζω (strengthen) to describe God as one who will "strengthen, establish, and ground" believers, the same word Jesus used in his commission to Peter.
In [ref:Apg 14:22|Acts 14:22], Paul and Barnabas strengthen the disciples' souls and encourage them to hold fast to their faith, a parallel to Jesus' commission to strengthen the brothers.
In [ref:Apg 18:23|Acts 18:23], Paul travels through Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening (στηρίζω) all the disciples, as a parallel to the commission Jesus gave Peter.
